chapter: New York, Nick's and the Army
title: Brad Gowans, Jimmy Ryan's and the start of the Commodore records
summary: He plays with multi-instrumentalist Gowans, works Sundays at Ryan's, and Milt Gabler begins recording him for Commodore.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah - okay---(end of Tape 2 - SIDE ONE)
Yeah and Brad played the clarinet and I played the trumpet and we played the old-- we did the Dixieland... many things -- we did (demonstration of music done) -- what was that? She danced to it.
No - no -- well, she did two Dixie-Land songs but she came out and did a fantastic dance -- now we were doing that show and doubling at Nick's. Now,

just before we got into there - because, you know, I was playing Sunday afternoons at Jimmy Ryan's and doing all those things and it was at this time that Milt [Gabler] that he wanted me to record--- and, of course, you know the Commodore records that I've made and I even made one with Brad when we -- what was left of the Original Dixie-Land Jazz Band--- and we did the jazz band things and Brad played the clarinet. It always amazed me to no end.
That he could play both instruments so well---
Yes and once -- I remember once he was having a problem with me, with a horn trying to get something -- so he just took the horn out of my hand and played it for me.
Your trumpet -- I mean your cornet?

Yes - he played it; he just could everything. And, he was a hell of an arranger on top of it you know. And, it was that time that Milt was getting interested in my recording--- for him and that's when all the recordings started. And, ---
